anchor: Special Campaign 6: institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency in government offices
argumentsAgainst: Campaign-based disposal can become a periodic compliance exercise unless simplification, record management and follow-up are embedded in routine administration.
The source records forwarding of one Parliamentary Assurance implementation report, but does not establish final closure of all targeted assurances.
argumentsFor: Targeted disposal of references, assurances, files and scrap can reduce administrative backlog and improve office functionality.
Review and weeding of records, space management and e-waste disposal connect cleanliness with administrative efficiency and environmental responsibility.
background: DIPAM is a department of the Ministry of Finance. The source states that it has no attached or subordinate offices or autonomous bodies.
The source describes a Preparatory Phase from 15 September 2026 to 30 September 2026 and an Implementation Phase from 2 October 2026 to 31 October 2026.
The campaign mechanism combined pendency reduction, procedure simplification, record review and weeding, cleanliness, space management and scrap disposal.
indiaImplications: Administrative departments can link cleanliness drives with measurable disposal of pending references and better record management.
The example illustrates how institutional accountability requires tracking both disposal targets and the quality or finality of outcomes.
E-waste disposal through an authorised institutional channel can support responsible asset and waste management, although broader environmental outcomes are not established by the source.

example.heading: Illustration: converting a campaign into routine governance
example.text: Suppose a department identifies pending references, reviews its records, removes files eligible for weeding under applicable rules, and tracks each remaining matter to closure. The illustration shows how a cleanliness campaign could create an administrative workflow; it is hypothetical and is not a reported event.

pocketRead.excerpt: DIPAM’s Special Campaign 6 combined cleanliness, pendency reduction, record management, space management and e-waste disposal in government-office administration.

question.answer: A durable model would connect target-setting with responsibility, documented disposal, review of records, monitoring of pending matters and outcome audits. This would prevent cleanliness from being reduced to a one-time physical exercise.
question.prompt: How can an office convert a cleanliness campaign into a durable governance reform?

sections.heading: From office upkeep to pendency management
paragraphs: DIPAM’s action during Special Campaign 6 shows a combined approach: administrative matters were identified for disposal while files, space and scrap were also managed. The mechanism is that less backlog and better-organised records can make routine decision-making easier.
The source does not establish that every targeted matter was finally resolved. Therefore, campaign reporting should distinguish disposal, forwarding for consideration and substantive closure.

sections.heading: Why institutionalisation matters
paragraphs: A campaign has practical value when its methods continue after the campaign period. Target registers, record-review rules, responsibility allocation and follow-up reviews can convert a temporary drive into regular administrative discipline.
For UPSC analysis, the central lesson is to connect Swachhata with probity, efficiency and accountability, while avoiding the misconception that physical cleanliness alone proves governance quality.

sourceTitle: DIPAM Participates in Special Campaign 6 for Institutionalising Swachhata and Minimising Pendency
staticDefinition: Institutionalising Swachhata means embedding cleanliness, record management, space management and responsible scrap disposal into regular office administration; minimising pendency means identifying and acting on pending official matters through defined targets and follow-up.
use: Use this as a governance and probity example to show how office cleanliness can be connected with pendency reduction, record management and accountable public administration.

advisory_notes: The claim that the campaign demonstrates environmental responsibility is reasonable analysis, but the source does not establish broader environmental outcomes.
The statement that better-organised records can make routine decision-making easier is an analytical inference, not a reported source fact.
The assertion that campaign methods should continue after the campaign period is normative advice rather than evidence about DIPAM’s later practice.
The proposed GS2.5, GS2.8 and GS4.6 codes are not standard official UPSC syllabus numbering; retain only if they are an internal taxonomy.
The use of “probity” is defensible through accountability and work-culture themes, but physical cleanliness alone does not establish probity.
The recall-card phrase “targeted VIP references and Parliamentary Assurances” is accurate but omits the release’s Inter-Ministerial and PMO references.
The pocketRead headline and deck accurately summarize the release, while the statement that cleanliness can create an administrative workflow is clearly labelled as an illustration.
The applied-question answer is sound analysis, but “outcome audits” and “routine governance” are recommendations, not documented DIPAM actions.

wayForward: Make campaign targets part of routine departmental work plans with named responsibility.
Distinguish disposal, forwarding, closure and rejection in monitoring records.
Use lawful record-retention and weeding procedures alongside digitisation and retrieval systems.
Conduct periodic outcome audits so reported activity is not treated as equivalent to substantive resolution.
